subject: Pricing & context-length profiling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + token/context profiling (next steps)

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can update the pricing quote for procurement.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + agent assist (real-time snippets + longer docs).
- Typical user flow: short prompt snippets for context + longer generated summaries on request.
- Desired context length options to evaluate: 8k (baseline), 32k (most likely), 128k (strategic/rare).

Requested profiling items for pricing (what I said we'd get back to you on):
1) Avg prompt tokens: you mentioned most sessions today are ~300-600 prompt tokens; some automated inputs push to ~2k.
2) Avg completion tokens: live summaries average 150-400 tokens; larger batch exports up to 4k.
3) Relative frequency: ~85% sessions fit within 8k, ~12% need 32k, ~3% would require 128k.
4) Monthly token volumes: you estimated 150M prompt tokens + 80M completion tokens as a base case (please confirm).

Action items for us (next steps):
- I attached the token profile template (acme_token_profile.csv) — please fill the "% sessions per context" column and send back so we can finalize unit economics.
- We'll iterate the quote (redwood_pricing_quote_v2.pdf) with per-1M-token pricing scenarios across 8k/32k/128k and quantization options.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min procurement sync next week to review the adjusted quote and procurement timeline.

High-level unit economics note (preliminary):
- Baseline (8k model, fp16): target competitive list price range ~$4,000–$6,500 per 1M tokens across prompt+completion (depends on batching & cache).
- 32k contextual variant: ~1.5–2x baseline price per 1M tokens (largely due to memory and lower throughput).
- 128k variant: 3–4x baseline price per 1M tokens unless heavily quantized or offloaded; expect higher per-token cost but lower incident rate.

Please confirm the monthly volume numbers and the % split per context length in the attached CSV. Once we have that we will produce a modeled quote showing target $/1M token line items and the recommended Dedicated vs Hosted deployment trade-offs.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_token_profile.csv, redwood_pricing_quote_v2.pdf

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + token/context profiling (next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and clarifications below.

Volumes we can confirm for modeling (rough, will validate with analytics team):
- Prompt tokens: 150M/month (90% regular, 10% elevated where automated context is appended).
- Completion tokens: 80M/month (mostly short summaries; occasional export jobs ~4k tokens but rare).
- Context length distribution: 8k = 82%, 32k = 15%, 128k = 3% (very rough).

Budget range: rough procurement target is $10k–$30k/month at first year ARR cadence; open to committed volume pricing if the unit economics model matches. Key ask: show us pricing that hits <= $12k/month for the baseline 8k workload under reasonable batching assumptions.

Two specific questions for your team:
1) Can you show a line comparing hosted (usage-based) vs Dedicated (reserved) costs at our volumes?
2) For the 32k and 128k options, list expected latency impact and whether quantized 4-bit models are an option for us (we care about response time for agent assist).

I'll fill the CSV this afternoon and send it back.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Johnson | Head of AI Products, Acme Corp
+1 212-555-0104

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme profiling — proposed unit economics (internal)

Internal summary and proposed figures to include in the updated quote (for Marissa to share):

Assumptions (model + perf):
- Baseline model: open-llm-8k (fp16) with standard batching; achievable throughput at 8k context ~8k tokens/s per GPU with continuous batching.
- 32k variant: same model architecture but longer attention memory; throughput drops ~40% vs 8k baseline absent additional GPUs.
- 128k variant: requires KV sharding / more memory; throughput drops ~65% without asynchronous offload.
- Quantization: 4-bit QAT or GPTQ gives ~1.8–2.5x cost reduction but may affect latency by 10–25% depending on kernel availability.

Modeled $/1M token ranges (final quote will be narrower):
- 8k, hosted (fp16): $4,500 per 1M tokens (batched, prefix caching assumes 25% cache hit for repeated prompts).
- 8k, hosted (4-bit): $2,300 per 1M tokens (if quality validated).
- 32k, hosted (fp16): $8,500 per 1M tokens.
- 32k, hosted (4-bit): $4,200 per 1M tokens.
- 128k, hosted (fp16): $15,000 per 1M tokens (rare ops, higher memory churn).
- Dedicated commit note: with a 12-month committed capacity (Reserved), you can expect ~25–45% reduction on hosted list depending on commit level and burst mix.

Suggested next step for quote: produce a modeled cost table for their confirmed monthly volumes (Sarah's numbers) showing: hosted fp16, hosted 4-bit, dedicated fp16 at 12mo commit. Add a column for expected avg latency (p50/p95) for the 3 context classes.

Marissa — happy to jump on the procurement call. Also suggest including a note on automatic fallback (32k -> 8k truncated variant) and fall-through pricing for cases where full 128k isn't needed.

-Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
